title: Colorectal Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for colorectal cancer. Full pathway by primary site (colon vs rectum), then workup -> pathologic / clinical stage -> risk- and biomarker-adapted adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy -> response reassessment -> surveillance, then a recurrence branch and a full metastatic line-of-therapy sub-tree (molecular workup -> resectability -> MMR -> RAS / BRAF / HER2 / sidedness -> first line -> response reassessment -> second line -> progression -> refractory / best supportive care). Every curative arm routes through adjuvant / response steps into surveillance; every advanced arm is refined by line of therapy before a recommendation. Treatment leaves reference APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by id; agents without a dose protocol (anti-EGFR, bevacizumab, encorafenib, HER2-directed antibodies, regorafenib / trifluridine-tipiracil / fruquintinib) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Invents no dose / regimen / criterion. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Colon / Rectal Cancer, DeVita, Harrison). Regimen leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses. No proprietary guideline text reproduced.

a.text: Universal MMR / MSI testing on all colorectal cancers screens for Lynch syndrome and predicts immunotherapy benefit; deficient-MMR stage II colon cancer has a favorable prognosis and derives little benefit from single-agent fluoropyrimidine.

b.text: Adjuvant oxaliplatin duration for stage III can be individualized (IDEA framework): 3 months of CAPOX for low-risk (T1-3 N1) is a reasonable option to limit cumulative neurotoxicity, versus 6 months for high-risk (T4 or N2).

c.text: Anti-EGFR antibodies (cetuximab / panitumumab) benefit only RAS wild-type (KRAS / NRAS exons 2/3/4) tumors and are most effective in left-sided primaries; they are ineffective or harmful in RAS-mutant disease and less effective in right-sided tumors.

d.text: Nonoperative watch-and-wait management after a clinical complete response to total neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer requires strict protocolized surveillance; it is an organ-preservation option that carries a local regrowth risk and is not standard for every patient.

e.text: After ~4-6 months of induction doublet, de-escalation to fluoropyrimidine (5-FU / leucovorin or capecitabine) with or without bevacizumab as maintenance limits cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy while preserving disease control; reintroduce the full doublet on progression.

f.text: Refractory-line oral agents (regorafenib, trifluridine-tipiracil with or without bevacizumab, fruquintinib) and biomarker re-use strategies (bevacizumab beyond progression, ctDNA-guided anti-EGFR rechallenge in RAS wild-type) have no dose protocol here and are shown as agent-level guidance; clinical-trial enrollment is encouraged.

nodes.name: Primary site
nodes.title: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: primary site
nodes.description: Management branches first by primary site - colon versus rectum - because the rectum sits within a bony pelvis and often needs neoadjuvant therapy that colon cancer does not.
bullets: Colon (cecum to sigmoid): surgery first, then risk-adapted adjuvant chemotherapy
Rectum (within ~15 cm of the anal verge): pelvic MRI drives neoadjuvant sequencing
Either site with M1 disease routes to the shared metastatic line-of-therapy pathway

nodes.name: Colon workup
nodes.title: Colon: workup
nodes.description: Confirm the diagnosis, complete colonic evaluation, and establish stage and tumor biology before deciding on adjuvant therapy.
bullets: History and physical; colonoscopy with biopsy confirming adenocarcinoma; clear the whole colon (repeat within 3-6 months if obstructing)
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis with contrast for staging; baseline CEA
Universal MMR / MSI testing on the tumor (Lynch screen + immunotherapy predictor)
Extended molecular panel (RAS, BRAF-V600E, HER2) if metastatic or if metastatic disease is anticipated
CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel; surgical / anesthesia fitness assessment

nodes.name: Colon stage
nodes.title: Colon: stage and risk stratification
nodes.description: Resected pathologic stage (pTNM) directs adjuvant therapy; clinically metastatic disease routes to the systemic pathway.

tables.title: Colon cancer: stage groups and adjuvant intent (AJCC TNM, simplified)
rows: Risk-adapted; observation vs adjuvant fluoropyrimidine +/- oxaliplatin

nodes.name: Stage I colon
nodes.title: Stage I colon: surgery alone
nodes.description: Complete surgical resection is curative; no adjuvant chemotherapy is indicated.
bullets: Colectomy with regional lymphadenectomy (>= 12 nodes) to negative margins
No adjuvant chemotherapy
Proceed to standard surveillance

nodes.name: Stage II risk
nodes.title: Stage II colon: high-risk features and MMR
nodes.description: Stage II benefit from chemotherapy is small and confined to higher-risk, mismatch-repair-proficient tumors. Classify by high-risk features and MMR status.
bullets: High-risk features: T4 (pT4a/b), poorly differentiated / high grade (non-dMMR), lymphovascular or perineural invasion, bowel obstruction or perforation, < 12 nodes sampled, positive margin
dMMR / MSI-H stage II has an excellent prognosis and does not benefit from single-agent fluoropyrimidine
Consider a validated recurrence assay / ctDNA to refine the small absolute chemotherapy benefit

nodes.name: Stage II observe
nodes.title: Stage II colon: observation (low-risk or dMMR)
nodes.description: Low-risk or dMMR / MSI-H stage II colon cancer: surgery with observation; chemotherapy is generally not recommended.
bullets: Curative resection already performed; no adjuvant chemotherapy
Shared decision-making: for high-risk pMMR only, single-agent capecitabine may be discussed (modest, uncertain benefit)
Proceed to surveillance

nodes.name: Stage II high-risk adjuvant
nodes.title: Stage II colon, high-risk pMMR: adjuvant chemotherapy
nodes.description: High-risk, mismatch-repair-proficient stage II colon cancer: consider adjuvant fluoropyrimidine, with oxaliplatin for the highest-risk features (e.g. T4).
bullets: Fluoropyrimidine alone (infusional 5-FU / leucovorin or capecitabine) for high-risk disease without T4
Add oxaliplatin (FOLFOX; or CAPOX described as guidance) for T4 or multiple high-risk features
Duration up to ~6 months; weigh oxaliplatin neurotoxicity against small absolute benefit
Regimens referenced below; the dose engine computes patient doses

nodes.name: Stage III duration
nodes.title: Stage III colon: IDEA risk group and adjuvant duration
nodes.description: Node-positive colon cancer receives adjuvant oxaliplatin-doublet chemotherapy; the IDEA framework individualizes duration by relapse risk to balance efficacy against cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy.
bullets: Low-risk (T1-3 N1): 3 months of CAPOX is non-inferior for most and limits neuropathy
High-risk (T4 and/or N2): 6 months of oxaliplatin-doublet is preferred
Patients unfit for oxaliplatin: fluoropyrimidine alone for ~6 months
Biologics (bevacizumab, anti-EGFR) have NO role in the adjuvant setting

nodes.name: Stage III low-risk 3mo
nodes.title: Stage III colon, low-risk: 3 months CAPOX (or 6 months FOLFOX)
nodes.description: Low-risk node-positive colon cancer: a shorter oxaliplatin-doublet course preserves efficacy while limiting neurotoxicity.
bullets: 3 months of CAPOX (capecitabine + oxaliplatin, described as guidance) for T1-3 N1
Alternatively 3-6 months of FOLFOX; stop oxaliplatin early for grade 2+ persistent neuropathy and continue the fluoropyrimidine
Then proceed to surveillance
FOLFOX / fluoropyrimidine backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Stage III high-risk 6mo
nodes.title: Stage III colon, high-risk: 6 months oxaliplatin-doublet
nodes.description: High-risk node-positive colon cancer (T4 and/or N2): a full 6-month oxaliplatin-doublet course is the standard adjuvant backbone.
bullets: 6 months of FOLFOX (or CAPOX as guidance) for T4 and/or N2 disease
Monitor cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy; hold oxaliplatin and continue fluoropyrimidine if grade 2+ persists
Then proceed to surveillance
FOLFOX backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Stage III fluoropyrimidine
nodes.title: Stage III colon, oxaliplatin-unfit: fluoropyrimidine alone
nodes.description: For patients unfit for oxaliplatin (pre-existing neuropathy, frailty), single-agent fluoropyrimidine retains meaningful adjuvant benefit.
bullets: Infusional 5-FU / leucovorin or capecitabine for ~6 months
No oxaliplatin (contraindicated by neuropathy or frailty)
Then proceed to surveillance
Fluoropyrimidine backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal workup
nodes.title: Rectal: workup
nodes.description: Local T and N staging by pelvic MRI is the pivotal step that determines whether neoadjuvant therapy is needed.
bullets: History and physical with digital rectal exam; rigid or flexible proctoscopy to measure distance from the anal verge
Colonoscopy with biopsy; CEA
Pelvic MRI (preferred) for T stage, mesorectal nodes, circumferential resection margin, and extramural vascular invasion
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis to exclude distant disease
Universal MMR / MSI testing; extended molecular panel if metastatic

nodes.name: Rectal stage
nodes.title: Rectal: clinical stage / risk
nodes.description: Clinical stage on MRI stratifies rectal cancer into early disease (surgery first) versus locally advanced disease (neoadjuvant first) versus metastatic.

tables.title: Rectal cancer: clinical risk groups and default sequencing
rows: Upfront TME (or local excision for select cT1)
cT3-4 and/or N+, or threatened CRM
Total neoadjuvant therapy or neoadjuvant chemoRT, then surgery

nodes.name: Early rectal
nodes.title: Early rectal (cT1-2 N0): surgery first
nodes.description: Clinically early rectal cancer is resected upfront; adjuvant therapy depends on final pathology.
bullets: Transanal local excision for highly selected cT1 N0 with favorable features; otherwise transabdominal total mesorectal excision (TME)
If final pathology is upstaged (pT3-4 or node-positive), give postoperative chemoRT + chemotherapy (or manage as locally advanced)
Proceed to surveillance

nodes.name: LARC neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Locally advanced rectal: neoadjuvant approach
nodes.description: Locally advanced rectal cancer is treated with neoadjuvant therapy before TME. Total neoadjuvant therapy (all chemo + RT before surgery) improves compliance and enables organ preservation; dMMR tumors may be treated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy.
bullets: Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT): long-course chemoRT (or short-course RT) plus consolidation / induction FOLFOX or CAPOX, then TME
Neoadjuvant chemoRT alone (capecitabine-sensitized long-course RT), then TME, then adjuvant chemotherapy
dMMR / MSI-H LARC: neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade can produce high complete-response rates and organ preservation
Selective non-radiation strategy (neoadjuvant FOLFOX alone) for lower-risk cT3 N0/N1 tumors with clear CRM

nodes.name: Rectal TNT
nodes.title: Rectal TNT: all systemic + RT before surgery
nodes.description: Total neoadjuvant therapy delivers radiation and full-course chemotherapy before TME, then response is reassessed.
bullets: Long-course chemoRT (capecitabine-sensitized) or short-course RT (5 x 5 Gy), sequenced with FOLFOX or CAPOX (induction or consolidation)
Consolidation TNT (chemoRT then chemotherapy) maximizes the clinical-complete-response rate for organ preservation
Reassess response at completion before committing to surgery vs organ preservation
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal chemoRT
nodes.title: Rectal neoadjuvant chemoRT then adjuvant
nodes.description: Capecitabine-sensitized long-course chemoRT, then TME, then adjuvant chemotherapy to complete perioperative treatment.
bullets: Long-course pelvic RT with concurrent capecitabine (radiosensitizer)
TME ~8-12 weeks after chemoRT
Adjuvant FOLFOX (or CAPOX as guidance) to complete ~6 months of perioperative chemotherapy
Reassess response before surgery
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal dMMR IO
nodes.title: Rectal dMMR / MSI-H: neoadjuvant immunotherapy
nodes.description: Deficient-MMR locally advanced rectal cancer is exquisitely immunotherapy-sensitive; neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade can yield durable clinical complete responses and rectal preservation.
bullets: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade (checkpoint inhibitor) for dMMR / MSI-H LARC
High rate of clinical complete response supporting non-operative organ preservation
Reassess response before deciding surgery vs watch-and-wait
Immunotherapy dosing referenced below

nodes.name: Rectal reassessment
nodes.title: Rectal: response reassessment after neoadjuvant
nodes.description: After neoadjuvant therapy, restage (DRE, endoscopy, pelvic MRI) to decide between TME and protocolized organ preservation.
bullets: Clinical complete response (cCR): no visible / palpable tumor, normal MRI / endoscopy - candidate for watch-and-wait
Residual disease: proceed to total mesorectal excision
Frank progression / distant spread on restaging: enter the metastatic pathway

nodes.name: Watch-and-wait
nodes.title: Rectal cCR: organ preservation (watch-and-wait)
nodes.description: Nonoperative management with intensive surveillance after a clinical complete response, preserving the rectum.
bullets: Strict protocolized surveillance: DRE + endoscopy every 3-4 months and pelvic MRI for the first 2-3 years
Salvage TME on any local regrowth (usually still curable)
Reserve for informed patients able to comply with intensive follow-up
Proceed to standard surveillance in parallel

nodes.name: Rectal TME
nodes.title: Rectal residual disease: total mesorectal excision
nodes.description: Residual tumor after neoadjuvant therapy is resected with total mesorectal excision; complete any planned adjuvant chemotherapy.
bullets: Total mesorectal excision (low anterior or abdominoperineal resection) to negative CRM
Complete adjuvant FOLFOX / CAPOX if not fully delivered pre-op (TNT often completes chemotherapy before surgery)
Proceed to surveillance
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance after curative therapy
nodes.description: Structured follow-up after curative-intent resection to detect recurrence while still salvageable.
bullets: History, physical, and CEA every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6 months to 5 years
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis annually (more often for higher-risk stage III) for up to 5 years
Colonoscopy at 1 year (or ~6 months post-op if not cleared pre-op), then per findings; every 3-5 years thereafter
A rising CEA or new symptom triggers restaging
If recurrence is detected, enter the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: pattern
nodes.description: Distinguish isolated locoregional or oligometastatic recurrence (potentially curable with surgery) from widespread metastatic disease.
bullets: Biopsy to confirm recurrence; obtain / update the full molecular panel (MMR, RAS, BRAF, HER2)
Restage with CT +/- PET-CT; liver MRI if liver-limited disease is suspected
Re-testing may reveal actionable drivers not present at diagnosis

nodes.name: Locoregional recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated locoregional recurrence
nodes.description: Resectable isolated locoregional recurrence is managed with curative intent, then systemic therapy is considered.
bullets: Multidisciplinary review for resection; re-irradiation for pelvic recurrence if not previously irradiated
Perioperative systemic chemotherapy around resection
If unresectable or multifocal, manage as metastatic disease
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic workup
nodes.title: Metastatic: molecular workup
nodes.description: Metastatic colorectal therapy is biomarker-driven. Complete the full molecular panel and assess resectability before selecting first-line therapy.
bullets: MMR / MSI (dMMR / MSI-H predicts immunotherapy benefit)
Extended RAS (KRAS / NRAS exons 2/3/4) and BRAF-V600E
HER2 (ERBB2) amplification / overexpression; NTRK fusion in RAS/BRAF wild-type
Primary tumor sidedness (left = splenic flexure to rectum; right = cecum to transverse)
CT chest / abdomen / pelvis; liver MRI and multidisciplinary review if liver- or lung-limited disease may be resectable

nodes.name: Resectability
nodes.title: Metastatic: resectability
nodes.description: Liver- or lung-limited oligometastatic disease may be curable with metastasectomy; widespread disease is treated with palliative systemic therapy directed by biomarkers.

nodes.name: Metastasectomy
nodes.title: Resectable metastases: perioperative chemo + metastasectomy
nodes.description: Curative-intent resection of liver- or lung-limited metastases, framed by perioperative chemotherapy.
bullets: Perioperative FOLFOX (about 3 months pre and 3 months post) around metastasectomy, or upfront resection then adjuvant chemotherapy
R0 metastasectomy of liver / lung disease; two-stage or staged resection as needed
Convert borderline-resectable disease with intensive first-line therapy (see biomarker leaves), then re-evaluate for resection
After curative metastasectomy, resume standard surveillance; on later relapse re-enter this pathway
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below
nodes.linkLabel: After curative metastasectomy, resume standard surveillance

nodes.name: Metastatic MMR
nodes.title: Metastatic: MMR / MSI status
nodes.description: Deficient MMR / MSI-high metastatic disease is treated with first-line immunotherapy; proficient MMR disease is chemotherapy-based and directed by RAS / BRAF / HER2 and sidedness.

nodes.name: Metastatic dMMR 1L
nodes.title: Metastatic dMMR / MSI-H: first-line immunotherapy
nodes.description: First-line PD-1 blockade is preferred for deficient-MMR / MSI-high metastatic colorectal cancer and outperforms chemotherapy.
bullets: Single-agent pembrolizumab (PD-1 blockade) is preferred first line (KEYNOTE-177)
Dual checkpoint blockade (nivolumab + ipilimumab) is an alternative immunotherapy option
Reserve chemotherapy for immunotherapy-refractory disease
Watch for pseudoprogression; confirm progression before switching
Immunotherapy dosing referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic molecular
nodes.title: Metastatic pMMR: RAS / BRAF / HER2
nodes.description: For proficient-MMR metastatic disease, actionable drivers (BRAF-V600E, HER2 amplification) and RAS status direct targeted therapy layered on a chemotherapy backbone.

nodes.name: Metastatic BRAF 1L
nodes.title: Metastatic BRAF-V600E: first line
nodes.description: BRAF-V600E confers a poor prognosis; first-line therapy is an intensive chemotherapy backbone, with targeted BRAF / EGFR blockade held for progression.
bullets: First line: chemotherapy backbone (FOLFOX / FOLFIRI, or FOLFOXIRI in fit patients as guidance) +/- bevacizumab
Anti-EGFR monotherapy is ineffective in BRAF-V600E disease
Plan early biomarker-directed second line given aggressive biology
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic HER2 1L
nodes.title: Metastatic HER2-amplified (RAS wild-type): first line
nodes.description: HER2 amplification is an actionable target; first line is standard chemotherapy, with HER2-directed therapy typically reserved for later lines.
bullets: First line: standard chemotherapy backbone +/- bevacizumab
Avoid anti-EGFR antibodies in HER2-amplified tumors (predict poor benefit)
Reserve HER2-directed therapy (trastuzumab + tucatinib / pertuzumab, or trastuzumab deruxtecan) for later lines
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Metastatic RAS-mut 1L
nodes.title: Metastatic RAS-mutant: first-line chemo + bevacizumab
nodes.description: RAS-mutant disease is not a candidate for anti-EGFR therapy; first line is a chemotherapy doublet with bevacizumab.
bullets: FOLFOX / CAPOX or FOLFIRI + bevacizumab first line (FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab, as guidance, for fit high-burden patients)
NO anti-EGFR antibody (ineffective / harmful in RAS-mutant disease)
Bevacizumab is added as guidance (no dose protocol here)
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Sidedness
nodes.title: Metastatic RAS / BRAF wild-type: primary sidedness
nodes.description: In RAS / BRAF wild-type disease, primary tumor sidedness selects the first-line biologic: anti-EGFR for left-sided primaries, bevacizumab for right-sided.

nodes.name: Left RAS-wt 1L anti-EGFR
nodes.title: Left-sided RAS / BRAF wild-type: first-line chemo + anti-EGFR
nodes.description: Left-sided RAS / BRAF wild-type disease derives the greatest benefit from anti-EGFR antibodies added to a chemotherapy doublet.
bullets: FOLFOX or FOLFIRI + an anti-EGFR antibody (cetuximab or panitumumab) first line
Anti-EGFR is guidance only (no dose protocol here)
Bevacizumab + doublet is an acceptable alternative
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Right RAS-wt 1L bevacizumab
nodes.title: Right-sided RAS / BRAF wild-type: first-line chemo + bevacizumab
nodes.description: Right-sided primaries respond poorly to anti-EGFR therapy; a chemotherapy doublet with bevacizumab is preferred first line.
bullets: FOLFOX / CAPOX or FOLFIRI + bevacizumab first line
Anti-EGFR is less effective for right-sided tumors and is not preferred here
Bevacizumab is guidance only (no dose protocol here)
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: Metastatic: response after first-line therapy
nodes.description: Restage after ~4-6 months of first-line therapy. Response determines whether to attempt conversion surgery, de-escalate to maintenance, or move to second line.

tables.title: Metastatic colorectal: line-of-therapy sequencing
rows: Biomarker-directed doublet + biologic (or IO for dMMR)
Fluoropyrimidine +/- bevacizumab; reintroduce doublet on progression
Switch backbone; add / switch biologic by biomarker

bullets: Deep response / conversion: reassess liver- or lung-limited disease for metastasectomy
Response or stable disease: de-escalate to maintenance to limit cumulative toxicity
Progression on first line: proceed to second-line selection

nodes.name: Conversion metastasectomy
nodes.title: Converted to resectable: metastasectomy
nodes.description: A deep response to intensive first-line therapy can render initially unresectable liver- or lung-limited disease resectable with curative intent.
bullets: Multidisciplinary re-evaluation for R0 metastasectomy after maximal response
Do not over-treat before surgery (avoid excess hepatotoxicity / vanishing lesions); operate at best response
Consider perioperative continuation of the effective backbone after resection
After curative resection, resume standard surveillance; on later relapse re-enter the metastatic pathway
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below
nodes.linkLabel: After curative conversion resection, resume standard surveillance

nodes.name: Maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance after first-line induction
nodes.description: After induction response, de-escalate to fluoropyrimidine-based maintenance to limit cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy while preserving disease control.
bullets: Fluoropyrimidine (capecitabine or infusional 5-FU / leucovorin) +/- bevacizumab as maintenance
Drop oxaliplatin after ~4-6 months or for grade 2+ persistent neuropathy
Reintroduce the full induction doublet on progression before declaring true second line
On confirmed progression despite reintroduction, proceed to second-line selection
Maintenance fluoropyrimidine backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Second-line selection
nodes.title: Metastatic: second-line selection
nodes.description: On progression, switch the chemotherapy backbone and choose the biologic / targeted layer by biomarker and prior exposure.
bullets: Switch backbone: FOLFIRI after FOLFOX (or FOLFOX after FOLFIRI)
Continue / switch the biologic by RAS status (bevacizumab beyond progression, or anti-EGFR if RAS wild-type and not yet used)
BRAF-V600E: encorafenib + cetuximab; HER2-amplified: HER2-directed therapy
dMMR progressing on immunotherapy: switch to a chemotherapy doublet + biologic

options.label: RAS wild-type, anti-EGFR not yet used

nodes.name: 2L anti-EGFR
nodes.title: Second line: switch backbone + anti-EGFR (RAS wild-type)
nodes.description: For RAS wild-type disease not previously exposed to anti-EGFR, add cetuximab or panitumumab to the alternate chemotherapy backbone.
bullets: FOLFIRI (or FOLFOX if not used first) + anti-EGFR antibody
Anti-EGFR is guidance only (no dose protocol here)
Confirm ongoing RAS wild-type status (consider ctDNA before rechallenge)
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: 2L BRAF targeted
nodes.title: Second line: encorafenib + cetuximab (BRAF-V600E)
nodes.description: After first-line chemotherapy, BRAF-V600E disease is treated with BRAF + EGFR blockade.
bullets: Encorafenib + cetuximab (BRAF + EGFR blockade); no dose protocol here - agents only
Anti-EGFR monotherapy remains ineffective without BRAF blockade
May combine with a chemotherapy backbone in selected fit patients (guidance)
Optional chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: 2L HER2-directed
nodes.title: Second line: HER2-directed therapy (HER2-amplified, RAS wild-type)
nodes.description: HER2-amplified RAS wild-type disease is treated with HER2-directed regimens after first-line chemotherapy.
bullets: Trastuzumab + tucatinib, trastuzumab + pertuzumab / lapatinib, or trastuzumab deruxtecan; no dose protocol here - agents only
Avoid anti-EGFR antibodies in HER2-amplified tumors
Optional chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: 2L switch backbone
nodes.title: Second line: switch backbone + biologic
nodes.description: For RAS-mutant disease or after anti-EGFR exposure, switch the chemotherapy backbone and continue an anti-angiogenic biologic.
bullets: FOLFIRI after FOLFOX (or FOLFOX after FOLFIRI) + an anti-angiogenic biologic
Bevacizumab beyond progression, or aflibercept / ramucirumab with FOLFIRI (guidance only, no dose protocol here)
NO anti-EGFR in RAS-mutant disease
Chemotherapy backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Second-line progression
nodes.title: Metastatic: progression after second line
nodes.description: On progression after second line, fitness and performance status determine whether to offer refractory-line systemic therapy or transition to best supportive care.
bullets: Fit (ECOG 0-1), organ function preserved: refractory-line oral agents or a clinical trial
Declining performance status: best supportive care and symptom-directed measures
Reassess goals of care and palliative-care involvement at each transition

nodes.name: Refractory line
nodes.title: Metastatic: refractory-line therapy
nodes.description: Chemorefractory disease in fit patients is treated with oral multikinase / antimetabolite agents or biomarker re-use strategies, ideally within a clinical trial.
bullets: Regorafenib, trifluridine-tipiracil (+/- bevacizumab), or fruquintinib; no dose protocol here - agents only
ctDNA-guided anti-EGFR rechallenge for RAS wild-type disease with cleared resistance clones (guidance)
Tissue-agnostic options: larotrectinib / entrectinib for NTRK fusions; targeted therapy for rare drivers
Continue best supportive care and enroll in a clinical trial where available
Trifluridine-tipiracil dosing referenced below; regorafenib / fruquintinib remain agent-level guidance

nodes.name: Best supportive care
nodes.title: Metastatic: best supportive care
nodes.description: For patients with declining performance status not fit for further systemic therapy, care focuses on symptom control and quality of life.
bullets: Symptom-directed palliative care: pain, obstruction, bleeding, nutrition
Palliative interventions as needed (stent / diverting stoma for obstruction, palliative RT for bleeding or pain)
Early palliative-care integration and advance-care planning
No further cytotoxic therapy; reassess if performance status recovers
